candidates.name: GovConInABox federal award histories by vendor (Element Biosciences, Ultima Genomics, Complete Genomics/MGI, compared with Illumina)
candidates.access: Open the public profile page; no login needed. I opened it and confirmed it works. It lists 24 Element awards totalling $3.46M, last award 12 Nov 2025, with 13 visible rows. Examples: USDA 1232SA25P0384 'AVITI sequencing cartridges' $198K (12 Sep 2025); USDA 1232SA25P0356 AVITI WGS sequencer $308K (23 Sep 2025); USDA 12905B24P0183 AVITI 2x150 kits $216K (19 Aug 2024); HHS 75D30124P19808 AVITI $257K. Next, find the matching profiles by searching the site for 'Ultima Genomics', 'Complete Genomics' and 'Illumina'. Then open each award ID on USAspending's public award page (https://www.usaspending.gov/award/CONT_AWD_<PIID>_...) to read 'extent competed' and 'reason not competed'.
candidates.rationale: This is a new mirror; the HigherGov and USAspending API routes in the registry were blocked. It shows federal research labs (USDA ARS, CDC/HHS) moving consumables spend to Element kits in 2024-25, not just buying the instruments. If competition fields show 'competed' or 'lowest price', that is direct evidence of research buyers choosing on price. A year-by-year count of agency kit orders across Illumina and rivals would quantify how research-consumables share is leaking.

candidates.name: NSF Award Search API: Major Research Instrumentation (MRI) sequencer awards by platform, 2023-2026
candidates.access: Free GET API, no login. I confirmed it works: keyword=AVITI returns award 2511003, 'MRI: Track 1 Acquisition of Element AVITI System' at the University of Idaho, $584,845, starting 15 Sep 2025. Multi-term OR queries return 0, so run single keywords one at a time: AVITI, 'Element Biosciences', Ultima, DNBSEQ, NovaSeq, NextSeq, 'Illumina', 'sequencer'. Add dateStart=01/01/2023 and printFields=id,title,awardeeName,startDate,fundsObligatedAmt,abstractText. Then tally MRI sequencer awards by vendor and year, and grep the abstracts for 'cost', 'affordable', 'per base' and 'reagent'.
candidates.rationale: MRI proposals are the most price-constrained research capital purchases. A rising non-Illumina share of NSF-funded sequencers from 2024 to 2026, with abstracts justifying the choice on running cost, would be hard evidence that research buyers choose on price. The street has not looked at this source.

candidates.name: Leibniz Institute on Aging (FLI Jena): award notices for Illumina sequencing-chemicals purchases (a time series)
candidates.access: Public PDFs, found in search. Also: .../public_allocations/AS_16-2022_Lieferung_von_Sequenzierchemikalien_Veroeffentlichung_verg._Auftrag.pdf. A December 2025 notice ('45135150_Verbrauchsmaterialien_Illumina_Info_vergebener_Auftrag.pdf', negotiated award under UVgO to Illumina GmbH, delivery Dec 2025 to Jan 2026) was in a search snippet, but its user_upload URL returned 404. Look for it under the same public_allocations folder, or search the site with site:leibniz-fli.de 'vergebener Auftrag' Sequenz. The PDFs are compressed, so extract the text locally with pypdf in isolated mode.
candidates.rationale: German institutes must publish every award with its value and procedure. Three or more notices from one research buyer (2022, 2024, 2025) give a same-buyer series of Illumina consumables spend and procedure type. It would show whether spend is falling as volume holds, and whether institutes are moving from negotiated sole-source buys to price competition.

candidates.name: UC campus 'Approved Recharge Rate List' PDFs (annual, campus-wide, including genomics cores)
candidates.access: Public PDF, found in search. Fetch the 2025-26 list and the 2024-25 and 2026-27 versions (same path with the year changed). Then search the other campus budget offices: '"Approved Recharge Rate" 2026-27 genomics' with site:ucsd.edu, site:ucdavis.edu, site:ucsf.edu and site:berkeley.edu. Compare the sequencing-lane and per-sample rates year over year, and note any line items that were dropped.
candidates.rationale: These are official rate approvals, not marketing pages. They show whether research cores are passing on Illumina's falling $/Gb or absorbing funding cuts. Rates falling faster than vendor list prices would point to pressure from buyers or competitors. Cuts to subsidies or services would show funding stress. A multi-year, multi-campus panel goes beyond the single-core snapshots already known.

candidates.name: UK contract aggregator ukspending.com: supplier pages for Element Biosciences, Illumina Cambridge and MGI/Complete Genomics
candidates.access: Open web, no login; I opened it and it works. The contract shown is Aston University to Illumina Cambridge, £282,662, published 11 Feb 2026, and the page has 'View contracts' links for each supplier. Browse the supplier pages for Element Biosciences, MGI Tech, Complete Genomics and Illumina Cambridge, and list every 2025-26 award with buyer, value and date. Then cross-check the ones that matter on Contracts Finder via search snippets, since the official site returns 403.
candidates.rationale: This aggregator is not in the registry; bidsfactory was the one already used. It lets you count UK research awards going to non-Illumina vendors against Illumina in 2025-26, and compare instrument values (for example a £290K Element award against a £283K Illumina box). That would show whether competitive tenders by UK universities are pulling price.

candidates.name: University of Georgia GGBC core news archive: price cuts justified by researcher surveys
candidates.access: Public HTML. The article 'spring-forward-with-lower-prices-at-the-georgia-genomics-and-bioinformatics-core' is undated, so get its date from the archive page https://dna.uga.edu/2025/03 or from the WordPress REST API at https://dna.uga.edu/wp-json/wp/v2/posts?search=price, whose 'date' and 'modified' fields hold the timestamps. Walk all 2025-26 posts for lane-price changes and any notes on outsourcing or vendors.
candidates.rationale: I confirmed the post cites demand from a survey of researchers: 'Recent surveys of UGA researchers revealed a strong demand for more cost-effective genomics options.' It cut library prep to $20 per sample (full plate). This core is the one behind the Georgia expert call, so its dated public price moves would turn hearsay into a documented record of an academic buyer base forcing price cuts.

candidates.name: Core subsidy-cut notices (University of Nebraska BORC and peers), 2025-26
candidates.access: Public HTML, seen in a search snippet. The 2025 notice cuts subsidies: NPOD/pilot from 50% to 40%, non-NPOD NU investigators from 20% to 10%, linked to sustainability after NIH Phase 3 funding ends in 2029. Widen with the search '"subsidy" (reduced OR "no longer") "sequencing" core fees 2026 site:.edu', and also check https://biotech.unl.edu/single-cell-genomics/service-fees.
candidates.rationale: When subsidies are cut, the full price lands on investigators. That is the mechanism by which tight funding turns into price-elastic, discount-seeking research demand. A tally of dated subsidy cuts shows funding stress moving through to sequencing demand, which supports the 'fight on price' claim. Expect only modest quantification.

candidates.name: Mercell Nordic tender search for 2025-26 sequencer and consumables awards (non-Illumina winners, lowest-price criteria)
candidates.access: Public Mercell tender pages, which are indexed in several languages. Run these searches: 'site:mercell.com sequencing 2025 award', 'site:mercell.com AVITI', 'site:mercell.com DNBSEQ', 'site:mercell.com NovaSeq X'. The UiO NSC Illumina-consumables framework (2017, about 1.4M, 2+1+1 years) is the baseline and should have been re-tendered since about 2021. Look for its successor notice and whether the new framework was opened to multiple platforms.
candidates.rationale: A national core re-tendering its Illumina-only consumables framework as a multi-vendor or price-scored competition would be strong evidence. If the successor is still a direct award to Illumina, that is lock-in evidence against the thesis. Payoff is uncertain because the Nordic search results were thin.
